# SEO-082: Reference the sitemap index from the robots.txt of the host it covers

This page is generated from the canonical JSONL registry record. Edit the JSONL record and run `npm run docs -- --write`; do not edit this file directly.

## Statement

The robots.txt file names its sitemap or sitemap index with an absolute URL, and that URL is on the same host that served the robots.txt.

## Rationale

The Sitemap directive is how a crawler finds the submission without being told, and a directive pointing at a different host describes a file the crawler will not treat as authoritative for this one.

## Applicability

```json
{
  "all": [
    "public_site"
  ],
  "any": [
    "has_sitemap"
  ]
}
```

## Implementation

Emit the directive from the same configuration that decides the production origin, so the two cannot drift. When several sitemaps exist, name the index rather than listing each child file.

## Verification

- Level: `SOURCE_AND_RUNTIME`
- Method: Read the Sitemap directives out of the served robots.txt, then request each named URL and record its host and status.
- Evidence: `ROBOTS_TXT`, `SITEMAP`, `HTTP_STATUS`
- Automated check: `robots-sitemap-reference`

## Scope

- Search surfaces: `GOOGLE_SEARCH`, `BING_SEARCH`
- Frameworks: `any`
- Caution: none recorded.
